weeks.conclusion: Watch whether Android agents develop explicit permission models and reproducible task evaluations rather than accumulating integrations alone. The creative-skill wave should separate durable tools from prompt packaging as users demand measurable fidelity, provenance, and repeatability. Reverse-engineering interfaces are likely to keep expanding, but trust will depend on showing how conclusions were derived. November's next phase should be judged by whether oversight begins catching up with reach.
weeks.gaps: Agent observability is the largest absence: there is no visible new cluster for action logs, permission boundaries, rollback, or behavioral testing, despite both press concern and increasingly consequential mobile access. Provenance is also thin. Creative skills and reference galleries can generate or transform assets, yet licensing, source lineage, and output attribution are not a visible technical theme. The sample also underrepresents robotics and scientific tooling relative to industry coverage, and shows little new work on energy or cost measurement for autonomous workflows. Finally, local-first assistants are appearing, but interoperable identity and policy controls across models and devices are not. Those missing layers will determine whether portable skills become dependable infrastructure or merely convenient demos.
weeks.signal: The credible signal is clustered, bounded work. Android agents appear in independent implementations, skill packaging spans several concrete outputs, and reverse-engineering tools target code, animation, and machines rather than an undefined universal assistant. [OpenBMB/MiniCPM-OCR](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-OCR) is especially legible: it names a constrained task and includes correctness assessment in its scope. The top-topic counts reinforce a broader base in developer tools and automation, while AI and agent topics remain a substantial but smaller subset. Attention metrics deserve skepticism. [deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype) reached 9,326 stars within roughly two days, an extraordinary launch that proves attention but not retention or technical maturity. [aschmelyun/print-my-profile-pic](https://github.com/aschmelyun/print-my-profile-pic) explicitly converts stars into a physical novelty and has only six forks, making it engagement theater rather than an engineering trend. The three pose-and-clothing galleries show genuine demand, but shared counts and overlapping assets weaken the claim of independent innovation. Trending repositories provide only lifetime stars because `stars_gained` is absent, so enormous totals for agent frameworks indicate ecosystem gravity, not weekly momentum. No clear star-farm or fork-inflation cluster matches the learned manipulation thresholds in the visible new cohort, but several launch curves still warrant follow-up.
weeks.summary: Agent skills moved into phones, design, and reverse engineering, but evaluation and real-time oversight still lagged behind autonomy.
weeks.title: Agent Skills Leave the Coding Sandbox

weeks.conclusion: Watch whether background agents acquire explicit approval policies and audit trails, rather than only more integrations. Mobile control is likely to keep expanding, but projects that make interruption and recovery first-class will be more consequential than another device wrapper. Agent-native creative systems have not peaked; their next test is interoperability among structured scenes, rendering engines, and review workflows. Native recompilation also merits attention if the cluster produces reusable tooling rather than isolated game ports.
weeks.gaps: Agent permissions remain the largest absence. The crawl shows tools that can run persistently and operate phones, but not a corresponding wave of policy engines, tamper-evident action logs, revocation controls, or standardized evaluations. That gap matters more as agents leave the coding sandbox. Energy-aware inference and memory efficiency are also missing despite heavy press attention to data-center constraints and full-stack codesign. Accessibility is another disconnect: GitHub elevated repository-level accessibility statements, yet no visible new-project cluster tackles accessible agent interfaces or adaptive creative tooling. Finally, industrial domains highlighted in the press—6G, semiconductor fabs, public infrastructure, and robotics—have little representation beyond early simulation-oriented tools.
weeks.signal: The strongest signal comes from independent projects converging on bounded action. Phone operation appears in two new implementations, and agent-oriented media production spans 3D modeling, rendering, film, avatars, and GIFs. These are more credible than claims of general autonomy because practitioners can inspect the device action or rendered artifact. [janestreet/agent_skills](https://github.com/janestreet/agent_skills) also indicates that the skills pattern persists, but its sparse crawl metadata is insufficient to infer enterprise adoption. Topic counts support a broader foundation in developer tools and automation—179 and 165 occurrences respectively—while AI, LLM, and agent topics are smaller at 41, 33, and 31. Several launches deserve skepticism. [worldonlyu/Google_AI_Pro_2Year_ZeroCost_Auto](https://github.com/worldonlyu/Google_AI_Pro_2Year_ZeroCost_Auto) combines a promotional entitlement claim, no license, and 3,288 stars with 1,208 forks; that is attention, not evidence of durable engineering value. [Minireel/HGhub](https://github.com/Minireel/HGhub) amassed 3,899 stars and 1,544 forks around a vaguely described third-party media client, leaving substance difficult to assess from the crawl. Neither matches the learned fork-inflation threshold, and the visible cohort shows no three-repository near-identical star cluster with negligible forks, so coordinated manipulation should not be asserted. Trending entries lack `stars_gained`; their enormous lifetime totals establish ecosystem gravity, not this week's momentum.
weeks.summary: Agents moved into phones and creative production, while runtime controls and trustworthy adoption metrics remained conspicuously thin.
weeks.title: Agents Leave the Screen, but Guardrails Stay Behind
